title: Lambda pick-path pilot kickoff
contextText: Kickoff for the pick-path optimisation pilot with Org Lambda Robotics. Sasha is our exec sponsor.

segments.text: Okay, I think everyone's here. Thanks for making the time. This is the kickoff for the pick-path pilot, so I'd like to cover scope, timeline and who owns what.
Great. For the record, I'm Sasha Example, VP of Operations at Org Lambda Robotics. I'm sponsoring this on our side.
And I'm Tobín Dummyson, I'm an engineer on the warehouse systems team. I'll be the day-to-day technical contact.
Pia Sample, engineering manager at Larkspur. I'll be staffing the team from our side.
Perfect. So the short version: we want to prove that re-ordering pick paths based on live order mix cuts walking distance for pickers.
Right, and I want to be clear on where. My preference is that we run this in Building 3 only. It's our most predictable site and the floor supervisors there are open to trying things.
Building 3 only works for us. Do we all agree on that as the scope?
Yes, Building 3 has the newest shelving too, so the location data is cleaner.
Then let's call it decided. Building 3 only for the pilot.
On timing, what are you telling your leadership?
The pilot is scheduled for Q1. That's what's in our operating plan and what the board has seen.
Q1 is tight but doable if we get the floor data early.
Which brings me to data. Sasha, can your team get us the current floor plans and the shelf location export?
Yes. I'll send the floor plans and the location export by next Tuesday.
Thank you. Pia, on our side?
I'll staff two engineers on this from the start of February. JD is one of them, the other I'll confirm this week.
Will they need access to the warehouse management system directly or can we work from exports?
Exports are fine for the first month. We don't want to touch production systems until we've earned it.
Good, because anything touching the WMS directly will need sign-off from the CIO eventually, and that takes weeks.
Understood. We'll plan around exports.
One more thing, and this is just how I work: I'd much rather get a short written update every Friday than another recurring call. My calendar is already a mess.
That's easy. Friday written updates it is.
Can I be copied on those? I'd like to see what the engineers are seeing.
Of course. Tobín, you'll be on every update.
Last thing from me, do we have a named person on your side for security questions?
Tobín can route those. He knows who to ask.
Great. So to recap: Building 3 only, target Q1, floor plans by next Tuesday, and Friday written updates. Thanks everyone.

note.body:
# Lambda pick-path pilot kickoff

**Date:** January 8
**Attendees:** Alma Mockwell (Larkspur Labs), Pia Sample (Larkspur Labs), Sasha Example (Org Lambda Robotics), Tobín Dummyson (Org Lambda Robotics)

## Summary

Kickoff for the pick-path pilot with Org Lambda Robotics. The goal is to show that re-ordering pick paths based on the live order mix reduces picker walking distance. Sasha Example, VP of Operations, is the executive sponsor; Tobín Dummyson, an engineer on the warehouse systems team, is the day-to-day technical contact.

## Decisions

- The pilot will run in **Building 3 only**, Lambda's most predictable site with the newest shelving and cleaner location data.
- The team will work from data exports for the first month rather than connecting to the warehouse management system directly.

## Timeline

Sasha confirmed that the pilot is scheduled for Q1; this is what appears in Lambda's operating plan and what their board has seen. Pia considers Q1 tight but achievable if floor data arrives early.

## Action items

- **Sasha Example** — send the Building 3 floor plans and shelf location export by next Tuesday.
- **Pia Sample** — staff two engineers on the pilot from the start of February (JD plus one more, to be confirmed this week).
- **Alma Mockwell** — send a short written update every Friday, copying Tobín.

## Notes

- Any direct integration with the warehouse management system will eventually need sign-off from Lambda's CIO, which takes weeks, so the plan avoids it for now.
- Sasha prefers a short written update every Friday over another recurring call.
- Tobín will route security questions to the right people at Lambda.
